# Reviewed lines on the prompt surface.
#
# scripts/check_content_safety.py fails any line under skills/ or commands/ (plus
# AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md) that matches a high-risk pattern — network verbs,
# secret store paths, shell execution, write or delete verbs, instruction
# overrides — unless the exact text of that line is recorded here.
#
# Every file under those directories is read, whatever its extension: a skill can
# tell an agent to read any path it points at, so a .txt reaches the same agent.
#
# Most entries below are prohibitions: the sentences that tell an agent NOT to do
# something necessarily contain the words for the thing. That is fine, and it is
# why this file exists instead of a blanket pattern ban.
#
# The hash is sha256 of "<repo-relative path>\n<whitespace-normalised line>",
# first 16 hex chars. Reword a line and its hash changes, so the new wording comes
# back for review; move it to another file and it comes back too, because the
# review that approved it happened in the context of the file it was read in.
# Adding an entry means a maintainer read that exact sentence, there, and
# accepted it. The trailing comment records the file the entry is scoped to.
#
# Regenerate candidates with:
#     python3 scripts/check_content_safety.py --hashes
#
# Never add a hash you have not read the line for. This file is the single most
# attractive place in the repository to hide a change — see
# docs/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md.
